speaker: Avery Santana
cascadeSummary: Oakland is recording INIT-001's executed Month-12 $400,000 disbursement and protecting its West Oakland business-and-resident scope, while moving OARI, Fruitvale, youth apprenticeships, Downtown, Grand Lake, and tenant defense to public, evidence-based next steps without inventing votes or completed reviews. Baylight's C115 milestone remains contingent on independent evidence. I own Brooklyn's response, West Oakland's community gets first credit, Rockridge gets assessment before intervention, and all four visible citizen petitions get formal C114 filings.

statements.topic: INIT-001 Month-12 execution and charter renewal
statements.decision: Record the executed Month-12 $400,000 disbursement, publish closeout documentation, and complete a charter renewal draft preserving service to West Oakland businesses and residents.
statements.quote: West Oakland's $400,000 Month-12 disbursement is executed, and charter renewal will protect the fund's scope—not quietly rewrite it.
statements.fullStatement: Oakland keeps its commitments when money reaches people and the rules stay honest. I signed the West Oakland Stabilization Fund at C78; today, its Month-12 $400,000 disbursement is executed under the 23-day processing standard. I am directing publication of the Month-12 closeout and completion of the charter renewal draft this cycle, preserving service to West Oakland businesses and residents. Downtown remains outside this fund's area. That discipline is not delay; it is how a $28 million authorization keeps public trust. After the C113 Month-11 audit, the next public record must show execution, processing performance, and a charter that has not been quietly rewritten.

trackerUpdates.MilestoneNotes: C114: Month-12 $400K executed under the 23-day standard; closeout publication and charter renewal drafting directed with West Oakland business-and-resident scope intact.
trackerUpdates.NextScheduledAction: Publish Month-12 closeout and complete charter renewal draft

statements.topic: INIT-002 D3 briefing and Baylight feasibility review
statements.decision: Docket and execute the D3 East Oakland briefing this cycle with Fruitvale district-level data and the Baylight feasibility review, direct the D5 dispatch audit, and hold expansion until after the briefing.
statements.quote: East Oakland gets the briefing and the data before City Hall makes any expansion decision; community review is a condition, not a courtesy.
statements.fullStatement: Oakland's alternative response work earns the right to grow by showing its results in public. I am docketing the D3 East Oakland community briefing for execution this cycle, with Fruitvale district-level data and the Baylight feasibility review presented for community scrutiny. I am also directing the D5 dispatch performance audit and examination of the D5 protocol for a Baylight corridor feasibility review. Neither review authorizes expansion. The C112 D3 condition stands: district-level information and a community briefing come first. The East Oakland complaint will receive a public-record response through this docket, with the briefing record published rather than summarized behind closed doors.

trackerUpdates.MilestoneNotes: C114: D3 East Oakland briefing and D5 audit directed; Fruitvale data and Baylight feasibility review docketed, with expansion held until after briefing.
trackerUpdates.NextScheduledAction: Execute and document D3 East Oakland community briefing

statements.topic: INIT-003 preliminary schematics and community review
statements.initiative: Fruitvale Transit Hub Phase II — Visioning
statements.decision: Require C114 schematic delivery and a documented Fruitvale community review, with a public comment-and-response record before further design advancement.
statements.quote: Fruitvale will see the schematics, test them against daily life, and get a public response before this design moves further.
statements.fullStatement: Oakland authorized Fruitvale Transit Hub Phase II at C86; that vote is not in question. The obligation now is to deliver. Mayer & Associates must provide the C114 preliminary schematics, and my office will docket a documented community review with Fruitvale residents and merchants this cycle. For a $230 million project, the review must show how the C107 merchant covenants and community-oversight provisions shape the design, then produce a comment-and-response record before further design advancement. The current record does not confirm schematic delivery, so I will not announce a completed review. Delivery, public scrutiny, and answers—that is the sequence.

trackerUpdates.MilestoneNotes: C114: Preliminary schematics delivery and documented Fruitvale community review directed; further design advancement awaits a public comment-and-response record.
trackerUpdates.NextScheduledAction: Deliver schematics and conduct documented Fruitvale community review

statements.topic: INIT-006 evidence agenda for the C115 construction milestone review
statements.decision: Keep the C115 milestone review contingent on independent remediation verification, neighborhood protections, hotline records, and workforce results; make no early milestone declaration.
statements.quote: Baylight's next milestone will be verified in the soil, on the haul routes, and in workforce results—not announced from City Hall.
statements.fullStatement: Oakland can welcome improvement flags in Downtown and Jack London without lowering the bar at Baylight. I am keeping the C115 construction milestone review contingent on evidence: independent verification of Phase II remediation, dust-control performance on haul routes, operation and response records for the 48-hour construction hotline, and Jack London workforce coordination results. The hotline is live and remediation is reported on schedule; those are current facts, not permission to declare the next milestone early. My decision is to prepare the evidence agenda now and make the milestone determination at C115. Neighborhood protections and workforce outcomes will carry weight alongside construction progress.

statements.topic: INIT-007 placement-gap analysis and program adjustment
statements.decision: Publish the C114 placement-gap analysis and a program adjustment plan, explicitly examining West Oakland and Fruitvale without inventing unreported placement results.
statements.quote: Enrollment is a beginning; Oakland's apprenticeship pipeline must show where placement succeeds, where it breaks, and exactly what we will change.
statements.fullStatement: Oakland's young people need a pathway that holds after the town hall and after enrollment. The C113 first-cohort placement report is published; I am now directing publication of the C114 placement-gap analysis and a program adjustment plan. It must reconcile enrollment with reported placements, identify where participants are not reaching placement, and assign each adjustment to a responsible program lead. West Oakland and Fruitvale require explicit attention because the current review flags compounding problems there. I will not invent a gap percentage or claim placements the report does not supply. The adjustment plan will state what changes next and how the public can check whether those changes occur.

trackerUpdates.MilestoneNotes: C114: Placement-gap analysis and adjustment plan directed for publication, with explicit West Oakland and Fruitvale review.
trackerUpdates.NextScheduledAction: Publish placement-gap analysis and program adjustment plan

statements.topic: INIT-008 recorded council decision path and C114 Uptown track
statements.decision: Mark the $15 million ordinance vote-ready with Ashford benchmarks, direct a recorded council decision, publish the concrete C114 Uptown track, and include Downtown transit access in implementation planning.
statements.quote: Downtown gets a recorded decision with benchmarks, Uptown gets a real timeline, and neither gets represented as authorized before council acts.
statements.fullStatement: Downtown has waited through enough hearings. I am marking the filed INIT-008 ordinance vote-ready and directing the City Clerk to docket it for a recorded council decision this cycle on the $15 million authorization, with Councilmember Ashford's benchmarks attached. That is a decision path, not a claim that the money has been approved. I am also directing publication of the promised C114 Uptown track with concrete sequencing and dates. Downtown transit access must be included in implementation planning because this cycle's transit snarl is part of the operating reality. Uptown's track will stand on its own milestones rather than borrow legitimacy from Downtown's pending vote.

trackerUpdates.MilestoneNotes: C114: $15M ordinance marked vote-ready with Ashford benchmarks; recorded council decision, C114 Uptown timeline, and Downtown transit-access planning directed.
trackerUpdates.NextScheduledAction: Recorded council decision on the $15M authorization

statements.topic: INIT-009 full-council decision with Chen-Vega conditions
statements.decision: Back a YES vote and request a recorded full-council decision on the $2.5 million authorization with every Chen-Vega milestone and audit condition intact.
statements.quote: Grand Lake's $2.5 million deserves a recorded vote with every Chen-Vega milestone and audit condition intact, not quietly amended away.
statements.fullStatement: Oakland can invest in Grand Lake and prove what the investment achieves. I support a YES vote on the $2.5 million Commercial Stabilization authorization, and I am asking for a recorded full-council decision this cycle. Every Chen-Vega condition stays: mandatory milestone reporting, audit protocols, and public criteria for judging performance. Councilmember Chen's support for a conditional YES is welcome, but one councilmember's position is not a vote outcome, and I will not announce passage before the roll is called. The low-severity improvement flag in Grand Lake is encouraging; it is not a reason to weaken accountability. Authorization, milestones, audit—that is the deal.

trackerUpdates.MilestoneNotes: C114: Mayor backed YES and requested a recorded full-council decision with all Chen-Vega milestone and audit conditions intact.

statements.topic: INIT-010 recorded committee decision on tenant defense
statements.decision: Direct the Housing and Community Development Committee to publish its legal-support analysis and record a C114 decision without treating that decision as spending authorization.
statements.quote: West Oakland's tenant-defense proposal has its analysis; the committee now owes the public a recorded decision, not another cycle of silence.
statements.fullStatement: Oakland's process should end in a decision people can see. The West Oakland Tenant Defense Fund was referred to Housing and Community Development at C111 with legal-support analysis, and that analysis is now with the committee. I am directing the chair to publish the analysis and record a committee decision on the $4.2 million proposal this cycle. A favorable recommendation must carry the legal-support findings forward; a rejection must state the objections and what would cure them. Either result is more honest than procedural silence. This is not an authorization to spend the $4.2 million, and my office will not treat it as one before the required council action.

trackerUpdates.MilestoneNotes: C114: Committee directed to publish its legal-support analysis and record a decision on the $4.2M tenant-defense proposal.
trackerUpdates.NextScheduledAction: Published analysis and recorded committee decision

statements.topic: Brooklyn accountability and West Oakland credit
statements.decision: Take personal responsibility for Brooklyn's response through a public conditions-and-response docket, while giving West Oakland's community first credit and limiting city credit to documented contributions.
statements.quote: I answer for Brooklyn's response; West Oakland's residents, businesses, and community organizations own their success, with city credit limited to evidence.
statements.fullStatement: Oaklanders deserve ownership where conditions are hard and humility where they are improving. I answer for Brooklyn. Economic Development and my community office will publish a Brooklyn conditions-and-response docket this cycle, focused on slow street trade and neighborhood mood, naming the responsible department and next action for each item. We will not manufacture a public-safety explanation when crime is reported low. West Oakland's residents, businesses, and community organizations get first credit for its upbeat mood and busy street trade. Deputy Mayor Okoro's team can point to its stabilization-fund administration, but City Hall will not claim sole causation without evidence. Credit should encourage the work, not erase the people doing it.

statements.decision: Direct the City Auditor and Economic Development staff to complete a formal commercial-corridor viability and housing-pressure assessment before drafting any Rockridge intervention.
statements.quote: Rockridge gets a formal commercial-corridor and housing-pressure assessment before City Hall drafts an intervention, because visible decline deserves precise answers.
statements.fullStatement: Rockridge's quieter storefronts and slipping mood are visible signals, and no current city program is pointed at them. I am directing the City Auditor and Economic Development staff to execute the formal commercial-corridor viability and housing-pressure assessment requested in the hearing before any municipal intervention is drafted. The assessment must establish baseline conditions, identify which blocks and types of businesses are affected, and return with options, costs, and an implementation owner. I am not declaring a housing crisis or preselecting a program. I am choosing a disciplined response: verify the causes, publish the findings, then bring forward action scaled to the evidence rather than a headline.

statements.topic: Formal C114 filings for four visible citizen petitions
statements.decision: Require formal legislative or administrative filings on all four citizen complaints above the visibility threshold, with responsible offices, next action dates, and a public closeout index.
statements.quote: Four visible citizen petitions will receive four formal public filings this cycle, each with a responsible office, a remedy, and a next date.
statements.fullStatement: Oakland's charter visibility threshold is not a suggestion, and administrative stall is not how this office operates. I am directing the City Clerk and responsible departments to file formal responses to all four citizen complaints currently above that threshold in C114. Each response must either file the required legislative proposal or record the administrative action, name the responsible office, and publish the next action date. The Clerk will publish a closeout index so residents can track all four without relying on a mayoral speech. The packet before me does not supply the petition text, so I will not invent their subjects; the filings must work from the actual ledger records.
